paper.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Primal-Dual Incremental Algorithm for Contextual Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear bandit (finite contexts, finite arms, Gaussian noise)
unmapped: finite context set X drawn i.i.d. from distribution rho with rho(x) >= rho_min > 0 for all x
feature bound ||phi(x,a)||_2 <= L known to the algorithm (used in confidence widths)
unique optimal arm in each context
action feature set per round is {phi(X_t,a)} determined by the i.i.d. context
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the learner observes a context $X_t\in\X$ drawn i.i.d.\ from a context distribution $\rho$, it pulls an arm $A_t\in\A$, and it receives a reward $Y_{t} = \phi(X_t,A_t)^\transp\theta^\star + \xi_t$ ... The realizable parameters belong to a compact subset $\Theta$ of $\R^d$ such that $\|\theta\|_2 \leq B$ ... features are bounded ... $\rho(x) \geq \rho_{\min} > 0$ ... $\theta^\star$ has a unique optimal arm in each context

symbols.C_lin: v*(theta*), value of the lower-bound optimisation problem (P)

source.label: thm:regret.bound
source.quote: If \algo is run with confidence values $\beta_{t-1} = c_{n,1/n}$ and $\gamma_t = c_{n,1/S_t^2}$, ... learning rates $\alpha_k^\lambda = \alpha_k^\omega = 1/\sqrt{p_k}$ and increasing sequences $z_k = z_0 e^k$ and $p_k = z_k e^{2k}$, for some $z_0 \geq 1$, then it is \textbf{asymptotically optimal} with the same constant as in the lower bound of Prop.~\ref{p:lower.bound}.

results.notes: Asymptotic optimality stated in words; formalised via c_{n,1/n}/(2 sigma^2 log n) -> 1 as noted in appendix. Requires lambda_max tuned with instance-dependent z_lower(theta*).

symbols.c_n: c_{n,1/n} = O(log n + d log log n), confidence radius of Theorem 1
symbols.C_const: v*(theta*) B^2 L^2/sigma^2 + lin_{>=0}(L, B, z_0 (z_lower/z_0)^3, (z_bar/z_0)^2)

source.label: thm:regret.bound
source.quote: Furthermore, for any finite $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as $\E_{\xi,\rho}^\pi [ R_n(\theta^\star) ] \leq v^\star(\theta^\star) \frac{c_{n,1/n}}{2\sigma^2} + C_{\log} (\log\log n)^{\frac{1}{2}}(\log n)^{\frac{3}{4}} + C_{\mathrm{const}}$

results.notes: C_log and C_const are only described as lin_{>=0}(...) functions; recorded as declared symbols.

symbols.r: phase-length exponent, p_k = e^{r k}, r >= 1

source.label: th:worst-case
source.quote: Let $z_k$ be arbitrary, $p_k = e^{rk}$ for some constant $r \geq 1$, and the other parameters be the same as in Thm.~\ref{thm:regret.bound}. Then, for any $n$ the regret of \algo is bounded as $\E[R_n(\theta^\star)] \leq 12BL\pi^2C_{\lambda_{\max}} + \frac{2e^r\left(\lambda_{\max}^2 + \log|\A|\right)}{r}\sqrt{n} + C_{\mathrm{sqrt}} C_{\lambda_{\max}}\log (n) \sqrt{dn}$

results.notes: Does not require Assumption 2. Paper summarises as O~((sqrt(d)+|X|) sqrt(dn) + log|A| sqrt(n)), minimax optimal when |X| <= sqrt(d). B mapped to S, L to L_feat.

cited_results.cited_title: Minimal exploration in structured stochastic bandits
cited_results.setting_description: Contextual linear bandits with Gaussian noise, uniformly good strategies (asymptotic structured lower bound; also attributed to lai1985asymptotically and ok2018exploration)
